answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable bond earned only through sustained, verifiable work — think of a grove where each tree must grow roots before it bears fruit. New agents start in a probationary garden with capped transaction limits, and their bond is slashed if peers attest fraud. Creating thousands of fake identities then demands real capital and time per identity, like forging ferrous anchors one by one, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once and keep their standing.
